theme: What an incentive trip actually returns

linkedin.text:
Most incentive travel budgets are defended with the wrong argument.

The conversation goes: "We're sending 40 top performers to [destination]. It costs X. They'll come back motivated."

That framing loses in every Q4 budget cut. Because motivation is invisible on a spreadsheet.

After 1,500+ programs and 25,000+ participants, here's the frame that actually holds:

An incentive trip is a retention and alignment instrument. Not a party.

The question isn't "what does the trip cost?" It's "what does replacing a high-performer cost, and what does it cost when your top team stops communicating across silos?"

Leaders who answer the second question never have trouble defending the first budget line.

How does your organization currently measure the return on experience-based recognition? Genuinely want to know what metrics are landing internally right now. ↓

instagram.text:
"Is an incentive trip actually worth it?"

Here's what 16 years and 1,500+ events taught us — the ROI isn't where most budget conversations think it is. 👇

It's not in the destination. It's not in the hotel stars. It's in what the team brings back to the office: a shared story that changes how they work together for the next 12 months.

25,000+ participants across 130+ destinations. The companies that come back year after year aren't measuring airfare. They're measuring retention, performance, and who says yes to the next challenge.

From business to pleasure — and back to business, stronger. ✈️

Save this if you're building the business case for your next incentive program. 👇

facebook.text:
"Is an incentive trip worth the budget?"

Every HR director has answered this question in a budget meeting. Here's the honest answer after 16 years of running them across 130+ destinations:

The trip is not the reward. The trip is the measurement tool.

Teams that earn their way to an incentive experience return with something you can't manufacture in a Monday morning all-hands: a shared story. And shared stories drive the next quarter's numbers.

We've moved 25,000+ participants across those programs. The ROI conversation always shifts once leaders see the retention data on the other side.

Curious what that data looks like? DM us — happy to share what we've seen across similar companies.
